note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on Tuesday 5 May 1936 and there was no contest in any division: the Unionists nominated for the 21 divisions in which they held majorities and the Nationalists for ten, and the retiring members for the divisions without a nomination were deemed re-elected (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9; Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5). Polling in County Tyrone was fixed for Wednesday 3 June 1936; no poll was needed. The new council first met on Monday 8 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 13 June 1936, p. 5). The changes printed were Glenlark (Solomon Morris for Daniel M'Crea), Bencran (Fred M'Ivor for J. M'L. Armstrong) and Gortin (H. Miles for John Turner) (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9; Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1936, p. 9); the Ulster Herald (9 May 1936, p. 5) adds Patrick Quinn for B. Donaghey and John J. Colhoun for J. A. V. Mitchell. Division inferred from the 31 May 1933 return (Bernard Donaghey; Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6); the Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5 names Patrick Quinn as returned in place of Mr. B. Donaghey. The Belfast News-Letter and Mid-Ulster Mail list only three changes and do not name this one. Mr. Patrick Quinn spoke for Carrickmore at the council meeting of 13 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 20 June 1936). He was again returned for Carrickmore in 1939. Returned unopposed.
